subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finbot.ai>, Elena Gomez <elena@finbot.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so everyone is aligned and we can move toward a mutual action plan. I’ve summarized the pain, success criteria, and next steps below.

Pain points we heard
- Unit economics are the single biggest blocker: your average cost per generated token on your current hosted endpoints is ~4x what the product team expects for the forecasted volume.
- Latency spikes during peak trading hours cause a small but high-impact user experience regression.
- Current stack is fragmented: mix of AWS Lambda calling vendor hosted endpoints + an internal PyTorch/ONNX batcher running on EC2 for heavy jobs — no unified routing or efficient KV/prefix caching.

What success looks like for FinBot
- Reduce inference cost per active user by at least 50% while keeping 95th pctl latency within current SLOs (sub-500ms for user-facing generation).
- Predictable monthly spend tied to committed throughput (helps with forecasting).
- Gradual rollout to production with rollback and A/B metrics visibility.

Technical notes / constraints
- Open to model quantization and 4-bit/8-bit profiles if output quality remains within tolerance for the risk-detection classifiers.
- Strong preference to keep PII out of vendor logs; VPC/private deployment may be required for production.
- Want batching/caching logic that can be tuned per-route (chat vs risk classification).

Proposed next steps
1) I’ll send a short MLP cost model for Redwood vs current spend (attached) — Marissa (today).
2) Engineering sync with Dylan & FinBot infra to walk through request distribution and KV cache opportunities (target: next Wed).
3) Pilot scope: 2-week POC on a sample high-volume route (~50k req/day) with quantization profile + caching (target start: 2 weeks out).
4) Draft commercial/commit terms for Dedicated capacity if pilot meets economics (Monica to lead).

Attachments: redwood-cost-model-v1.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

If I missed anything or you want this adjusted, let me know — otherwise I’ll book the engineering sync after Samir confirms availability for next Wed (Mar 10).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

--
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference platform for production LLMs

From: Samir Shah <samir@finbot.ai>

Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures the discussion. A few clarifications:

- The ~4x figure is based on our current vendor invoices (avg token cost) + non-user facing preprocessing overhead. We can share detailed invoices and a small sample of traffic patterns offline.
- Quantization openness: our ML lead (Elena) is cautious — acceptable if we keep a held-out eval set for the high-risk classifiers and monitor regression closely.
- VPC is non-negotiable for production; for a POC we can run on a customer-managed subnet if Redwood supports it.

Confirming availability: Wed Mar 10 at 11am PT works for our infra folks.

Samir
